subject: Chat filters, channels, and menu-chat vocabulary
claim: The repository identifies typed chat, quick chat, quick-chat text, and core-emote messages, but the r806919 meanings of the chat filter byte, channel or audience fields, menu-chat identifiers, and client/server validation boundaries remain unverified.
how_to_repeat: Use two disposable accounts, two operator-owned client installations, and a private loopback Ambrose server with both clients in the same zone; do not use public services or reuse credentials.

Build a metadata-only inventory of the operator-owned QuickChat.xml entries, recording only entry counts, identifier names or hashes, and duplicate or invalid-id results. Do not copy client text, XML, archives, or extracted rows into the repository.

Send one ordinary typed line, one quick-chat selection, one quick-chat text entry, and one core emote from client A while client B observes. Record only message names, direction, service/order, frame order, field names, lengths, filter-byte values, source and destination field presence, and the visible result category.

Repeat each message with A and B in the same zone, different zones, and different visibility or range positions where the local server supports it. Record which audience receives the event and whether the sender is echoed.

For typed chat, vary exactly one safe input at a time: ordinary text, command-prefix text, an overlong line, and a line containing a locally configured blocked term. Record accept, refusal, command routing, truncation, or broadcast metadata without publishing the text.

For menu chat, send one valid identifier and one locally generated invalid identifier, then compare the client-visible result and server response. Do not infer the vocabulary or its meaning from a third-party list.

If private captures or screenshots are reduced for review, remove message text, account names, identifiers that identify a person, credentials, addresses, payload bytes, and client content; publish only metadata and outcomes. Rotate or destroy disposable credentials and delete private artifacts after review.
evidence: The phase 6.03 roadmap defines separate typed-chat, quick-chat, quick-chat-text, and core-emote messages and requires range filtering, command-prefix routing, ignore-list behavior, and quick-chat ID validation.
The same roadmap explicitly marks the typed-chat byte encoding, the Filter byte meaning, and the CORE_EMOTE Name=Chat behavior as unverified.
The contributor track lists F-32 because moderation needs the filter levels, channels, and menu-chat vocabulary before the server can validate them safely.
The current checkout has no implemented ChatHandler or ChatMgr behavior and no public protocol finding establishing channel or filter semantics.
No client-derived QuickChat.xml content or private two-client chat capture is available in the repository to establish the vocabulary or audience rules.
disproof: A maintainer-reviewed two-client experiment and metadata-only QuickChat inventory establish the valid menu-chat identifiers, filter and channel meanings, encoding boundaries, audience rules, and rejection behavior; that evidence should replace this gap record with verified per-message findings.
